sentences.text: The friend known as Rat and his good friend went to visit a wealthy man.
This man had a big house near the river.
His name was Toad.
Toad had grown very bored of small boats during recent months.
Instead, he had fallen completely in love with a large, beautiful vehicle.
This vehicle was painted in many bright colors.
It was a house on wheels which people usually pull with a strong horse.
Toad happily persuaded his two friends to take to the open road with him.
They set off together with a strong horse and a small van.
Camping and singing filled their days as they traveled along the bright country path.
All was happy until a fast machine passed them very quickly.
The loud vehicle frightened their poor horse significantly.
Then, the sudden movement tipped the little van right into a deep hole beside the path.
Rather than being upset, Toad sat in the middle of the road completely happy and full of interest.
From that single moment, he could think of nothing else.
He wanted nothing more than owning a fast machine of his own.
He gave a small hint about the trouble still to come in the future.
The open road was calling him toward new adventures.
He knew that his life would change forever.
His friends looked at Toad while he sat on the ground.
They knew that something strange had happened to him.
Toad did not care about the broken van at all.
He only thought about the fast machine that had passed them.
The beautiful vehicle had gone away down the road.
Toad stayed in the same place for a long time.
His friends tried to talk to him, but he did not listen.
He dreamed about the road and the fast machines.
Life would never be the same for him again.
They had to leave the broken van behind them.
Walking back home took many hours.
During the walk, Toad spoke only about fast machines.
He decided that he must buy one as soon as possible.
His friends tried to stop him from having such ideas.
They knew that fast machines brought danger and trouble.
However, Toad would not listen to any advice.
His mind was completely changed by that single afternoon.
Days passed, and Toad stayed inside his large house.
He refused to see any visitors or friends.
Everyone in the village wondered what had happened to him.
The truth was simple.
Toad was planning to buy a fast machine.
He had already written letters to several people who sold such vehicles.
Money was not a problem for a wealthy man like him.
Soon, a large delivery would arrive at his front door.
The quiet life of the river bank was about to end.
New adventures waited for them just around the corner.
Toad would soon discover the power of the open road.
Nothing could stop him from reaching his new goal.
The sun shone down upon the green fields while he planned his future.
He imagined himself driving very fast across the whole country.
His friends hoped that he might change his mind again.
Yet they knew that hope was entirely dead.
Toad wanted only speed and excitement.
No power on earth could hold him back now.
The wonderful car would soon become his most prized possession.
He smiled at the thought of the coming journey.

sentences.text: The morning air carried the crisp scent of damp earth and river reeds as the Rat and his companion made their way across the green meadows.
They were bound for the grand estate of their wealthy acquaintance, a restless individual known to all as Toad.
Toad possessed a magnificent house situated conveniently near the winding river, yet his temper was notoriously fickle.
During the preceding months, he had grown profoundly weary of small river craft and ordinary boating excursions.
A sudden and total infatuation had seized his imagination, displacing every prior hobby with absolute finality.
This new obsession took the physical form of a remarkably large and colorful vehicle parked near the stables.
Painted in brilliant hues of yellow and red, it resembled a miniature house mounted securely upon heavy wooden wheels.
Such conveyances were ordinarily utilized by travelers and were designed to be drawn at a steady pace by a robust draught horse.
Toad had already acquired the necessary animal along with the gleaming van, leaving only companions missing from his grand design.
With characteristic enthusiasm, he immediately set about persuading his two visitors to abandon their quiet routines for the open road.
Not without a degree of quiet apprehension, the friends allowed themselves to be convinced by his energetic rhetoric.
They set off together on a bright morning, the strong horse stepping out willingly while the painted van creaked behind them.
Days of unalloyed pleasure followed as they meandered along sunlit country lanes beneath a vast and cloudless sky.
Cooking over open fires and singing traditional songs filled their afternoons with a rustic charm that felt entirely timeless.
Had any observer asked, they would have declared this nomadic existence to be the very pinnacle of earthly contentment.
All such idyllic notions, however, were shattered in less than a single breathless second by the approach of modernity.
A monstrous machine came roaring around a sharp bend in the lane, moving with terrifying speed and a deafening mechanical howl.
Before anyone could issue a warning, the magnificent vehicle rushed past in a dense cloud of dust and acrid blue smoke.
The massive draft horse reared violently in sheer terror, its eyes wide with panic as it threatened to snap the heavy traces.
The sudden, chaotic movement proved fatal to their peaceful journey, tipping the little van completely onto its side.
There it lay, ignominiously tilted into a deep drainage ditch beside the road, its cheerful paint scratched and dull.
Yet it was not the damage to his prized possession that occupied the owner's wandering attention at this critical juncture.
Far from being upset or dismayed, Toad sat squarely in the middle of the dusty road with a vacant, beatific smile upon his face.
He remained utterly transfixed, his entire soul absorbed by the vanishing cloud of dust left behind by the mechanical apparition.
From that single, defining moment, his capacity for rational thought was entirely captured by the concept of velocity.
He could think of nothing else, desiring above all else to possess a powerful motor car of his own design and speed.
As he gazed down the empty lane, he let slip a vague hint concerning the profound trouble that awaited them all in the future.
The open road was no longer a pleasant path for camping; it was now a summoning call toward untried and dangerous adventures.
Deep down, he understood with absolute certainty that his quiet existence had altered irreversibly within the space of a heartbeat.
His friends stood watching him from the grass, recognizing instantly that some fundamental shift had occurred within his volatile mind.
Toad showed not the slightest concern for the ruined van or the cargo scattered haphazardly across the grassy verge.
He remained seated in the dirt long after his companions began urging him to stand and inspect the structural damage.
To all spoken questions and practical suggestions, he offered only silence, lost entirely in feverish daydreams of grease and horsepower.
Life along the peaceful river bank would never resume its familiar rhythm once this fever had taken root in his spirit.
With heavy hearts, the two friends realized they had no choice but to abandon the broken vehicle right where it had fallen.
The long walk back to the river bank occupied many hours, punctuated only by Toad's incessant monologue concerning gears and acceleration.
He had already decided that a proper machine must be purchased before the current week drew to its inevitable close.
Knowing his impulsive nature intimately, his companions attempted to inject doses of caution and common sense into the conversation.
They pointed out the obvious hazards, the exorbitant costs, and the general unreliability of such complicated mechanical contrivances.
Not a single word of their prudent advice registered upon a mind completely sealed by the glamour of sudden speed.
Days bled into one another, and Toad remained strictly confined within the high walls of his expansive country house.
He steadfastly refused to admit visitors, barring even his closest friends from entering the grand front doors.
Throughout the neighboring village, speculation ran rampant regarding the mysterious seclusion of the local squire.
The reality, of course, was far more mundane than the rumors suggested; Toad was simply engrossed in correspondence with vehicle manufacturers.
He had already dispatched urgent letters backed by substantial deposits of money to various dealers operating in distant cities.
For a man of his vast financial resources, acquisition was merely a matter of writing the correct figures upon heavy paper.
Soon enough, a massive delivery would rattle up the gravel driveway, changing the domestic atmosphere of the estate forever.
The tranquil, predictable days of the river bank were drawing to a close, replaced by the imminent roar of cylinders.
New and turbulent adventures waited just around the corner, promising excitement that would surely test the patience of everyone involved.
Nothing on earth possessed the power to halt his headlong rush toward this glittering, mechanical obsession.
Outside his study window, the afternoon sun cast long golden shadows across the impeccably manicured lawns and green fields.
Inside, Toad smiled broadly as he imagined himself hurtling across the countryside at speeds that would shock the local farmers.
Though his friends privately hoped that exhaustion might cause him to abandon his reckless scheme, they knew such hope was entirely futile.
Speed had become his new religion, eclipsing every other interest he had ever cultivated during his comfortable life.
The magnificent car would soon arrive to become his most cherished possession, setting the stage for chaos upon the highway.
